content: Historical design intent: complete canonical JSONL sources should eventually support database reconstruction and canonical source-reference resolution after uncoordinated worktree deletion. That serializer, rebuilder, and reference resolver are not implemented. This planned architecture does not make current SQLite databases disposable or instruct agents to delete them. Current agents preserve databases and private/local state, capture through supported Kindex tools, commit matching .kin/config and .kin/index.json with code, and publish only explicitly selected shareable evidence with kin repo-memory publish. Prompting is not a recovery guarantee. Owner hold https://github.com/wandercom/kindex/pull/72#issuecomment-5973372280 corrects the earlier wording; see docs/canonical-knowledge-migration.md.
title: Planned canonical JSONL recovery architecture

content: Current workflow: inventory the selected database and project evidence; preserve databases, private/local state, and source bindings. Do not delete a database or worktree as cache or change audience to force publication. Selected repo-memory exports and summary indexes are not lossless backups. Report preserved coverage, missing knowledge, unsupported fields/types, and unresolved bindings. Complete migration is planned work. Its acceptance criteria include field-by-field record and relationship coverage, protected private sources, reconstruction, and source-reference consistency. Intentional exclusions must have explicit scope, reasons, consequences, and release notes; they do not justify unexplained ongoing loss. Updating Kindex or its instruction files performs no automatic migration.
title: Preserve existing databases pending complete migration tooling

content: Current repo-memory behavior refuses publication and import when both .kin/knowledge.json and .kin/knowledge.jsonl exist. Preserve both inputs and explicitly reconcile records into one artifact; neither takes precedence. The older PR69 JSON-precedence behavior was replaced in PR74. Repo-memory reads only its named knowledge artifact, not every .kin/*.jsonl note, and transports selected active public/team concepts, decisions, questions, and supported peer relationships into quarantine. Graph-transfer export/import filters extra to supported lifecycle keys and omits source_refs and operational metadata. Saved SQLite paths/UUIDs do not resolve canonical JSONL or rebind recreated graphs; preserve source databases. Historical expired-session bindings require verifiable reconstruction or an unresolved report. PR71 relationship-only learn now retains supplied sources on linked per-call learned-text documents, but does not close canonical recovery gaps. Snapshot merging can select one same-ID revision, so preserve input knowledge and do not claim lossless conflict archival.
title: Current evidence transport and recovery limitations
